title: Pyspark memory issue when joining and filtering two dataframes
question:
I am trying to join two dataframes in pyspark. One dataframe df_dsp_f contains approx 100,000 records. Another dataframe df_slv_f contains approx 99,800 records.

I am using databricks and a serverless cluster for compute.

Objective

To identify the records that are in df_dsp_f but NOT in df_slv_f and mark those records as "X" under a newly created column D_flag. Both the dataframes contain same columns.

For this I am using the below code:

##Repartitioning on a specific column##
df_dsp_f_p = df_dsp_f.repartition(2, "col_5")
df_slv_f_p = df_slv_f.repartition(2, "col_5")

##Join and then select only records with X##
df_del = df_dsp_f_p.alias("df1").join(df_slv_f_p.alias("df2"),\
         on = (F.col("df1.col_1") == F.col("df2.col_1")) & \
              (F.col("df1.col_2") == F.col("df2.col_2")), \
         how = "left").\
         select(F.when(F.col("df2.col_1").isNull() | 
                F.col("df2.col_2").isNull(), "X").\
         otherwise(F.lit("")).alias("D_flag")).filter(F.col("D_flag") == "X")

After this when I am simply running df_del.count() I am getting below error:

Job aborted due to stage failure: Task 0 in stage 2324.1 failed 4 times, most recent 
failure: Lost task 0.3 in stage 2324.1 (TID 4180) 
Reason: Command exited with code 134, sigabrt

I had checked the cardinality of each of the dataframes and based on that I had chosen repartition option.

Can someone give me a clue on how to fix this?

Update

I have made the joining part simplified.

df_del = df_dsp_f_p.alias("df1").join(df_slv_f.alias("df2"), 
        (F.col("df1.col_1") == F.col("df2.col_1")) \& 
        (F.col("df1.col_2") == \
        F.col("df2.col_2")), how = "left_anti")
df_del = df_del.withColumn("D_flag",F.lit("X"))

But no luck. Simple df_del.show() is showing the same above error.

Update

Finally it got resolved. It was a cluster issue. Serverless is not powerful for complex joins.
answer:
The error you are encountering,

" Command exited with code 134, sigabrt"

typically indicates an out-of-memory issue or a problem with the underlying infrastructure.

You can use Broadcast Join If one of your dataframes is small enough to fit into memory, You can use a broadcast join to improve performance and reduce memory usage. In your case, since df_slv_f is slightly smaller, you can broadcast it.

df_dsp_f_p = df_dsp_f.repartition(2, "col_5")
df_slv_f_p = df_slv_f.repartition(2, "col_5")
df_del = df_dsp_f_p.alias("df1").join(
    F.broadcast(df_slv_f_p.alias("df2")),
    (F.col("df1.col_1") == F.col("df2.col_1")) & 
    (F.col("df1.col_2") == F.col("df2.col_2")),
    how="left_anti"
)
df_del = df_del.withColumn("D_flag", F.lit("X"))
display(df_del)

Results:


col_1   col_2   col_5   D_flag
5   E   X5  X
4   D   X4  X

In the above code Repartitioning on a specific column Using broadcast join to optimize the join operation Adding the D_flag column

Also Consider that your serverless cluster has enough resources (memory and CPU) to handle the join operation. You can try increasing the size of your cluster.
